sentences.text: Misc. Appeal No. 6138 of 2022

Smt. Geeta And Others
 Versus
 Aamen Khan And Others
 Appearance:
Shri Abhishek Agrawal, learned counsel for the appella  Shri Sudarshan Pandit, learned counsel for the respond  ORDER Heard on I.A. No.8344/2022, which is an application for condonation of delay.
There is a delay of 41 days in fling the present appeal.
For the reasons stated in the application, I.A. No.8344/2022 is allowed and the delay in filing the appeal is condoned.
I.A. No.6192/2025, an application for urgent hearing also stands disposed of.
2. The appellants have filed this appeal being aggrieved by the award dated 15.07.2022 passed in MACC No.3060/2017 challenging the quantum of compensation.
3. The liability of the insurance company due to death because of the accident by the insured vehicle is not under dispute.

4. The short facts of the case are that on 13.08.2017 at around 10.30 p.m. Shivram @ Yuvraj was going along with his friend Deepak on motorcycle to Kastur talkies for some work and when they reached near Laabariya Bheru in front of Kastur talkies a dumper bearing registration number MP09-KC-3855 came from behind in a most rash and negligent manner and dashed into the motorcycle NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29036 2 MA-6138-2022 of Shivram because of which he sustained injuries on several parts of the body and he died on the spot because of the said injuries.
5. A claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act was filed before the claims tribunal for compensation for the death of Shivram by the present appellants/claimants.

The claims tribunal Smt. Geeta vs Aamen Khan on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132689343/
1 after considering the evidence available on record awarded a total sum of Rs.12,13,070/- out of which the amount of Rs.10,04,070/- was for loss of dependency.
6. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the amount of compensation is very less.
The deceased at the time of accident was 40 years of age and he was earning Rs.18000/- per month as a construction worker.
However, the claims tribunal did not believe the same and fixed his income at Rs.5950/- per month on notional basis.

He further submits that even this income at notional basis is not correct because at the relevant time the minimum wages for an unskilled labourer was Rs.7125/-
per month, thus, he prays for enhancement of the compensation by properly assessing the income of the deceased.

7. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/insurance company supports the findings of the award and points out that the claims tribunal in para 21 has considered the aspect of the income of the deceased and submits that there was not even single substantive evidence on record so as to demonstrate the work and the income of the deceased, hence, the claims tribunal has rightly assessed the income on notional basis.
He thus prays for dismissal of the appeal.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9.

On perusal of the record and the findings in the light of the same, this Court is of the considered view, the claims tribunal has rightly disbelieved the claim of the income of the deceased at Rs.18000/- per month.
The claimants have not NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29036 3 MA-6138-2022 brought anyone to prove the said claim.

There was no material at all for establishing that the deceased was working as a construction labourer and was earning Rs.18000/-
per month.

However, from the perusal of the guidelines issued by the State Legal Services Authority it is seen that at the time of accident i.e. 13.08.2017, the minimum wages for an unskilled labourer were Rs.7125/- per month which, in the considered view of this Court, should be taken as income of the deceased.

Consequently, the same is taken as income of the deceased and after applying the multiplier of 15 as applied by the claims tribunal and adding 25% in head of future prospects now the compensation for loss of dependency would come to Rs.12,02,281/- and after deducting already awarded amount of Rs.10,04,070/-, now the appellants are entitled for payment of Rs.1,98,211/-
over and above the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal.
This enhanced amount shall carry interest @6% per annum from the date of filing of the application before the claims tribunal.
10. With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands disposed of.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE N.R.
